stage1.impression: A warm, symmetrical golden-hour living room. The pair of green horn speakers reads at a glance and the green light thrown on the wall behind the credenza is a lovely, true detail. But it still reads as a careful CG interior. The sunlit wall, curtain and rug all flatten into the same featureless cream. The walnut credenza has smeared, stretched grain. The view out of the window is a dark, muddy strip. The product's greens are pushed to a neon lime by the very orange light.

blocking_9: Sunlit plaster shows real surface texture under the raking sun (lum_range >= 10 inside the sun patch [560,60,820,330]) instead of a flat 2.7 range
Highlights are not all stacked on one tone-mapper shoulder: the sunlit wall, curtain and rug must separate (wall sun median ~195-210, curtain and rug distinct)
The product reads close to its reference colour: the cover cloth disc within dE 6 of #6F7F66 on the shaded speaker, and the cabinet interior a pale tinted green, not lime (b_median > 70)
The credenza veneer reads as real walnut: continuous grain without horizontal smear bands
The window/exterior reads as a bright daylit outside (median >= 110), not a dark strip at the left edge
A calm, evenly lit wall area for the heading 'A pair of Poison.' that is not crossed by a hard light/shadow edge

defects.what: Sunlit plaster is dead flat (lum_range 2.7). No plaster grain under a 14 deg raking sun, so it reads as CG paint
Curtain (median 227), sunlit wall (222) and rug (221) all sit on the same highlight plateau: the tone-mapping shoulder compresses every sunlit surface to one value
Walnut credenza grain is stretched into horizontal streaks/bands (vertical profile swings 154-170 in regular stripes). Reads as a smeared texture, not veneer
The exterior through the glazing is a dark, muddy brown strip (median 56-61) beside a 222 sunlit wall. Implausible for the sun-side windows, and it makes a heavy black bar at the frame edge
Cover disc reads saturated yellow-green (100,122,64), dE 9.6 from the cloth reference #6F7F66 (right disc dE 10.5). The warm sun and the grade shift the product colour
Cabinet interior glows neon lime (100,131,48), dE 25 from the #B2C9A2 reference; right speaker dE 35. The batts read as lime blocks, not pale voile
The two horns read differently: left median 115 vs right 145, dE 11 vs 22 to #4C6A36. The pair does not look identical
The rug is the brightest mass in the lower third (median 221) and pulls the eye down away from the speakers. Its front edge is cropped by the frame bottom
The heading zone is split by a hard sun/shadow edge near x 850 (lum_range 106). Type set over the wall would straddle it
The turntable is tiny, glassy and nearly lost against the green wall caustic. It reads as clutter rather than a hero prop
The right mains lead and socket sit tight to the speaker edge in the shadow. Fine, but the cable has a CG-uniform look

changes.problem: Every sunlit surface sits on the same tone-mapper shoulder, so the wall, curtain and rug lose all texture and separation.

evidence.measured: sun-patch wall median 221.7, lum_range 2.7; curtain median 226.8; rug median 220.7

changes.expected: The sunlit wall drops to ~195-205 and comes off the shoulder so plaster and pile detail resolve. Shadows deepen slightly (fill lamps in c6 compensate).

changes.problem: The plaster shows no relief under a grazing sun, the clearest 'render' tell in the frame.

change.to: bump 1.2, tex_scale 1.0 (finer real-scale trowel marks), tint_mix 0.6 so the scan's own tonal variation shows

changes.expected: Visible soft trowel texture and slight tonal mottling in the sun patch. The edges of the window-light shapes pick up a fine grain.

changes.problem: The sun is so orange that the product's greens go lime and the cloth reads yellow-green, so the colour is not true.

evidence.measured: left cover disc (100,122,64), dE 9.6 vs #6F7F66; interior (100,131,48), dE 25 vs #B2C9A2; sunlit wall b_median 173 vs r 248

change.to: #FFE2BC, white balance set so the sunlit wall renders a warm cream (r-b gap about 50 rather than 75)

changes.expected: Still late afternoon, but the product greens move back toward their reference: the cover disc dE < 6, the interior a paler, cooler green.

changes.problem: The exterior through the glazing is a dark brown bar, which contradicts the bright sun pouring in and weighs down the left edge.

evidence.measured: median 60.7, p95 129.4, against an interior sunlit wall at 222

change.to: strength 3.2, rotation chosen so that sunlit foliage and some sky fill the visible pane, not the shaded trunks

changes.expected: A daylit, airy view outside (median ~110-140) that explains the sunlight, gives depth and lightens the left edge.

changes.problem: The walnut credenza grain is stretched into horizontal bands, so the veneer reads as a smeared CG texture.

evidence.measured: vertical profile alternates 154/170/153 in regular bands; visible horizontal streaks across all three doors

change.to: a real high-resolution walnut veneer scan mapped at true scale (about 0.6 m per tile), grain running continuously across the three doors (sequence-matched), with a slight clearcoat sheen

changes.expected: Continuous fine cathedral or straight grain with no banding. The credenza reads as furniture photographed, not textured.

changes.problem: The two speakers of the pair are lit very differently, so they read as two colours.

evidence.measured: right horn median 145 dE 21.8 vs left horn 115 dE 11.3 to #4C6A36; right interior dE 35 vs left 25

change.to: toe-in [6, -6] so both faces take the sun at a similar angle; north irradiance 0.7 to lift the shaded speaker's open shadows after the c1 exposure cut

changes.expected: Both horns within about 10 levels of each other in median, so the pair reads as identical.

changes.problem: The rug is the brightest mass in the bottom of the frame and pulls the eye from the speakers.

evidence.measured: median 220.7, as bright as the sunlit wall

change.to: value 0.45, tint #8E8170 (an oatmeal wool, a stop darker than the wall)

changes.expected: The rug settles a stop below the wall and becomes a base, not a competing highlight.

changes.problem: The heading's zone on the wall is split by a hard sun/shadow edge, so type over the wall would straddle it.

change.to: about -68 deg, so the window-light patch spans the upper centre of the wall (x 480-960) and the shadow edge moves right of x 1000

changes.expected: A continuous lit field across the upper centre for the heading, with the window shadows still raking across the right side.

out_of_scope.request: Give the cover cloth a visible woven texture; the disc reads as a flat painted circle (right disc lum_range 3.4)
out_of_scope.why: The cover is part of the speaker and the card fixes its parts and materials

out_of_scope.request: Make the internal batts and voile read as soft white textile rather than lime blocks beyond what lighting can do
out_of_scope.why: The cabinet's interior lining is part of the fixed speaker
